Considering California’s drought conditions, would this downpour be better for the drought than the same amount of rain occurring over a long period of time? Why or why not? ( 3 points ) a. No (1), rain spaced out over a long period of time would be better. When sudden downpours occur, the ground eventually becomes saturated and all other precipitation is unable to infiltrate into the ground (1). The major indicator of drought is soil moisture and once it becomes saturated, it can’t become moister. Essentially, all the other precipitation goes to waste. This is not the case with more spaced-out rain, as water is consistently able to infiltrate and replenish soil moisture (1).

answer_key_excerpt: Describe how each of these lakes likely formed based on their shape and other clues in the map. ( 4 points, 2 each ) Lake Baikal: Formed inside a tectonic rift (1) as it filled with water. Tectonic activity commonly creates long, thin lakes (1), as we see in Lake Baikal. Crater Lake: Filling of a volcanic crater/caldera (1). This is the most common formation method of nearly circular lakes, and we can tell the lake is surrounded by a mountain based on the radial drainage pattern around it (1).
